summary: In metropolitan France a captive-bred roof rat is legal to keep, hobby-breed, and give away, and the species-vs-domestication line does not, in practice, add a permit. The roof rat is non-domestic (the Arrêté du 11 août 2006 lists only 'les races domestiques du rat (Rattus norvegicus)' among the rodents), so it is governed by the Code de l'environnement and the Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018. But Annexe 2 of that order places Rattus rattus in the catch-all 'Toutes les autres espèces de Rodentia' row, which is column (a) 'Pas de formalité' (no formality) for 1 to 40 adult animals; only 41 or more triggers a certificat de capacité. Marking and I-FAP registration apply only to protected or CITES species (Article 3 of the same order), so they do not apply to the roof rat. A sale (vente) must come with a written document d'information (Art. L413-8); a free transfer between private persons does not. R. rattus is not on the EU Union list (Reg. 1143/2014) or France's metropolitan invasive Arrêté du 14 février 2018, so there is no keeping or sale ban. Commercial breeding or selling to the public is a separate, permitted-only regime (établissement authorization plus, for trade, Code rural Art. L214-6). Two limits: the species is managed as invasive in the French overseas territories (DROM-COM), where local decrees prohibit it; and the 2021 welfare law created a future 'positive list' (Art. L413-1A) whose implementing arrêté is still unpublished, a watch item rather than a current restriction.

keep.why: The roof rat is non-domestic (the Arrêté du 11 août 2006 lists only 'les races domestiques du rat (Rattus norvegicus)' among the Muridae), so it is governed by the Code de l'environnement (Art. L413-1 et seq.) and the Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018. Annexe 2 of that order places R. rattus in the catch-all row 'Toutes les autres espèces de Rodentia, hors espèces figurant en annexe A du règlement (CE) n° 338/97 susvisé et hors espèces protégées en application de l'article L. 411-1 du code de l'environnement', for which column (a) 'Pas de formalité' covers 'De 1 à 40' adults and only '41 et plus' triggers a certificat de capacité. So keeping 1 to 40 adult roof rats requires no declaration and no permit. Marking and I-FAP registration apply only to protected or CITES species (Article 3 of the order), not to R. rattus. The species is not on the EU Union list or the metropolitan invasive list, so there is no keeping ban. Overseas territories (DROM-COM) manage it as invasive and may prohibit it locally.
keep.governing_law: Arrêté du 11 août 2006 (domestic list, R. norvegicus only); Code de l'environnement Art. L413-1 à L413-5; Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018 (mod. Arrêté du 5 sept. 2025), Annexe 2, column (a) 'Pas de formalité' De 1 à 40; Article 3 (marking limited to protected/CITES).

breed.why: Non-commercial hobby breeding (élevage d'agrément) follows the same Annexe 2 thresholds as keeping: below 41 adult animals R. rattus sits in column (a) 'Pas de formalité', so no declaration and no breeding permit are required; offspring count toward the threshold only once adult. Reaching 41 or more adults moves the keeper into column (c), requiring a certificat de capacité (Art. L413-2) and an autorisation d'ouverture d'établissement (Art. L413-3). Breeding for profit or systematically producing litters for the public is a separate matter: it requires opening a declared establishment (autorisation préalable under Art. R413-8) and, as a pet-trade activity, falls under Code rural Art. L214-6. The L413-1A 'élevage de conservation' carve-out awaits its implementing decree.
breed.governing_law: Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018, Annexe 2 (column (a) 'Pas de formalité' De 1 à 40); Code de l'environnement Art. L413-2, L413-3, R413-8; Code rural Art. L214-6 (commercial); Loi 2021-1539 Art. 14 / Art. L413-1A.

sell_give.why: A private person may give away or sell a small number of captive-bred roof rats without a permit. The attestation de cession and identification-document formalities of Art. R413-23-4 apply only 'pour les animaux des espèces mentionnées à l'article L. 413-6' (marked, i.e. protected or CITES species), which R. rattus is not, so they do not bind a roof-rat transfer. A sale (vente) of a live non-domestic animal must be accompanied by a written document d'information on the animal's characteristics, needs, and upkeep (Art. L413-8); a gratuitous transfer between private persons does not require it. Selling commercially or systematically to the public requires operating a declared pet-trade establishment (autorisation préalable, Art. R413-8; Code rural Art. L214-6). R. rattus is not on the EU Union list, so there is no sale ban.
sell_give.governing_law: Code de l'environnement Art. R413-23-4 (cession formalities limited to L413-6 marked species), Art. L413-8 (document d'information on a sale), Art. R413-8 (establishment authorization); Code rural Art. L214-6 (commercial pet trade); Reg. (EU) 1143/2014 (R. rattus not on the Union list).

transport.why: Moving a captive-bred roof rat within metropolitan France is legal for private individuals, subject to humane, escape-proof transport. There is no EU pet-passport or harmonised health-certificate scheme for rodents (Reg. (EU) 576/2013 does not cover them), so intra-EU non-commercial movement follows the destination country's national rules. Importing from outside the EU triggers veterinary controls: the Arrêté du 19 juillet 2002 (Annexe 18 model certificate for rodents) requires a health certificate from an official veterinarian of the exporting country and presentation at an approved Border Control Post. R. rattus is not on the EU Union list or the metropolitan invasive Arrêté du 14 février 2018, so there is no import ban for métropole. The French OVERSEAS territories (Réunion, Mayotte, Martinique, Guadeloupe and others) manage R. rattus as a damaging invasive species and local decrees prohibit its introduction, detention, transport, and sale, so transport into or within those territories is unlawful.
transport.governing_law: Arrêté du 19 juillet 2002 (Annexe 18 model, rodent import health certificate); Reg. (EU) 576/2013 (does not cover rodents); Reg. (EU) 1143/2014; Arrêté du 14 février 2018, Annexe I (metropolitan invasive list, R. rattus absent); overseas prefectural/ministerial invasive-species decrees (DROM-COM).

restrictions.summary: Below 41 adult animals there is no formality: the roof rat falls in column (a) 'Pas de formalité' of Annexe 2 of the Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018. Reaching 41 or more adults moves the keeper into column (c), which requires a certificat de capacité and an autorisation d'ouverture d'établissement. The certificat de capacité is a professional-grade credential (theory dossier, logged practical experience, defence before a departmental commission, facility inspection), so the practical ceiling for a hobbyist is 40 adults.
steps: Stay at or below 40 adult animals to remain in the 'Pas de formalité' tier
To exceed 40 adults, obtain a certificat de capacité and an autorisation d'ouverture d'établissement
restrictions.where_to_file: Préfecture de département (DDETSPP / DREAL) for the certificat de capacité and establishment authorization

restrictions.summary: A sale (vente) of a live roof rat must be accompanied by a written document d'information on the animal's characteristics, needs, and upkeep (Art. L413-8). A free transfer between private persons does not require it. Selling commercially or systematically to the public requires operating a declared pet-trade establishment (autorisation préalable, Art. R413-8; Code rural Art. L214-6). The attestation de cession / I-FAP formalities of Art. R413-23-4 do not apply, because they are limited to marked (protected/CITES) species.
steps: On a sale, give the buyer a written document d'information (Art. L413-8)
Do not sell commercially or systematically without a declared establishment

restrictions.summary: Importing from outside the EU requires a veterinary health certificate (Arrêté du 19 juillet 2002, Annexe 18 model for rodents) issued by an official veterinarian of the exporting country, with presentation at an approved Border Control Post. There is no EU pet passport for rodents; intra-EU non-commercial movement follows the destination state's rules. Never release a roof rat into the wild.
steps: For non-EU import, obtain the Annexe 18 veterinary health certificate and clear an approved Border Control Post
For intra-EU movement, check the destination country's national rules for rodents
restrictions.where_to_file: Border Control Post (Poste de contrôle frontalier)

restrictions.summary: In the French overseas territories (DROM-COM: Réunion, Mayotte, Martinique, Guadeloupe and others) R. rattus is managed as a damaging invasive species and local prefectural/ministerial decrees prohibit its introduction, detention, transport, reproduction, and sale. The metropolitan 'no formality' position does NOT apply there.
restrictions.where_to_file: Préfecture / DEAL of the territory concerned

inquiry_focus: (1) Confirm that captive-bred Rattus rattus, as a non-protected, non-CITES rodent, falls under the 'Toutes les autres espèces de Rodentia' catch-all row of Annexe 2 of the Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018, placing 1 to 40 adults in column (a) 'Pas de formalité' (no declaration, no certificat de capacité), and that under Article 3 it is therefore exempt from mandatory marking and I-FAP registration. (2) The positive-list arrêté under Art. L413-1A (Loi 2021-1539) is not yet published. What is the timeline, and what is the procedure to formally request that captive-bred Rattus rattus be evaluated for inclusion as a companion species (and any grandfathering for existing pets if it is omitted)? (3) For intra-EU transport of a captive-bred R. rattus by a private individual with no change of ownership, is any documentation/notification required, and does TRACES apply to non-commercial movement?

sources.title: Arrêté du 11 août 2006, liste des espèces, races ou variétés d'animaux domestiques (Muridae: only 'les races domestiques du rat (Rattus norvegicus)'; R. rattus absent)
Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018, Annexe 2: 'Toutes les autres espèces de Rodentia' in column (a) 'Pas de formalité' De 1 à 40, 41 et plus = certificat de capacité (R. norvegicus = déclaration from 1)
Arrêté du 8 octobre 2018, Article 3: mandatory marking + national-file registration limited to L411-1/L411-2 protected and CITES (Reg. 338/97 Annexes A-D) species; R. rattus exempt
Code de l'environnement Art. R413-23-4: attestation de cession / identification document obligations limited to 'animaux des espèces mentionnées à l'article L. 413-6' (marked species)
Code de l'environnement Art. L413-8: 'Toute vente d'un animal vivant d'une espèce non domestique' must include a document d'information (applies to sales, not gratuitous gifts)

Code de l'environnement Art. L413-1 A: positive list for non-domestic companion animals fixed by arrêté du ministre chargé de l'environnement; 'toute personne physique ou morale' may request inclusion, reasoned reply within six months (arrêté still pending)
Code rural Art. L214-6: pet-trade establishment declaration (élevage / vente)
Regulation (EU) 1143/2014 on invasive alien species: Union list does NOT include Rattus rattus
Regulation (EU) 576/2013 on the non-commercial movement of pet animals: rodents not covered by the EU pet-passport scheme
Arrêté du 14 février 2018 (métropole), Annexe I: espèces exotiques envahissantes; 'Rattus norvegicus (Berkenhout, 1769): Rat surmulot' listed, R. rattus absent
Arrêté du 19 juillet 2002: conditions sanitaires pour l'importation d'animaux vivants (Annexe 18: rongeurs / rodents health certificate)
